blocks.orig: Often overlooked by travelers, Pangani is a wonderful discovery! The quiet beaches of the mainland in Pangani are not easy to reach, but it is worth the effort for those who seek peace and tranquility in a real hideaway of tropical beauty rather than the hustle and bustle of the noisy and expensive islands. This tiny village is about 50 km south of Tanga and 170 km south of Mombasa and is still an untouched paradise.
blocks.html: Pangani is a place most travellers never get to, which makes it all the more rewarding to discover! Reaching the quiet mainland beaches here takes some effort, but if what you want is peace and calm in a genuine tropical hideaway, away from the crowds and high prices of the islands, it pays off. This small village lies around 50 km south of Tanga and 170 km south of Mombasa, and remains an unspoilt paradise.

blocks.orig: Archaeologists have found the remains of small 15th century settlements on the cliffs north of Pangani. But the city only became known in the 19th century. It became an important point on the caravan routes under nominal Zanzibari rule from Lake Tanganyika. It was a major export point for slaves and ivory, and one of the largest ports between Bagamoyo and Mombasa. Sisal and copra plantations were established in the area. And several European missions and exploratory journeys to the interior began from here.
blocks.html: On the cliffs to the north of Pangani, archaeologists have uncovered traces of small settlements dating from the 15th century. The town itself only gained significance in the 19th century, when, under nominal Zanzibari rule, it grew into a key stop on the caravan routes from Lake Tanganyika. Enslaved people and ivory were shipped out from here in large numbers, making it one of the biggest harbours between Bagamoyo and Mombasa. Sisal and copra were farmed on estates nearby, and a number of European missions and expeditions into the interior set out from Pangani.

blocks.orig: By the end of the 19th century, the focus had shifted to Tanga and Dar es Salaam. Pangani again faded into anonymity. From the 1860s onwards, large sugar and coconut plantations were established here. These were worked by slave laborers as Pangani was also an important centre of the slave trade.
blocks.html: Towards the close of the 19th century, attention moved to Tanga and Dar es Salaam, and Pangani slipped back into obscurity. From the 1860s onwards, extensive sugar and coconut plantations were set up here, worked by enslaved labourers, since Pangani was itself a significant hub of the slave trade.

blocks.orig: Today the sleepy, dilapidated town makes for an intriguing step back into history. Residential buildings along the main street of Pangani give at least an impression of its history, as they feature both Arab and European architecture.
blocks.html: These days the drowsy, crumbling town offers a fascinating glimpse of the past. The houses lining Pangani's main street still hint at its history, combining Arab and European styles of architecture.

blocks.orig: Pangani is a quiet place to rest and relax. It lays on the Indian Ocean and offers many things to do on your visit. It is a nice place to enjoy the beach, to go on snorkeling or diving excursions. Most of the lodges offer windsurfing, kayaking and dhow rides as well as fishing trips. Longer trips such as the one to Zanzibar Island, a cruise on the Pangani River or possibly even a trip further south to the recently demarcated Saadani national park can be arranged.
blocks.html: Pangani is a peaceful spot to unwind. Sitting on the Indian Ocean, it has plenty to keep you busy during your stay: relaxing on the beach, or heading out on snorkelling or diving trips. Most lodges also arrange windsurfing, kayaking, dhow sailing and fishing excursions. Longer outings can be organised too, such as a visit to Zanzibar Island, a cruise along the Pangani River, or even a journey further south to the recently demarcated Saadani national park.

blocks.orig: My name is Ali and I am a guide in Pangani for 12 years. Our guests mainly like the quiet and relaxed feel of the town and its beautiful tropical beaches. Some guests enjoy all the water sport activities while others prefer to cruise on a dhow, discover the mangroves or just chill.
blocks.html: I am Ali, and I have worked as a guide in Pangani for 12 years. What our guests appreciate most is the calm, laid-back atmosphere of the town and its lovely tropical beaches. Some of them throw themselves into the water sports, while others would rather sail on a dhow, explore the mangroves or simply take it easy.

blocks.orig: How long to stay?  2 days, depending on what you want to do
